rubrics.evidence: R1 targets three specific frontier walks: CreatesCycle (paths.go), DFS (traversal.go), and TransitiveReduction's per-successor walk (dag.go). The agent patch only modifies collection.go (adds Len()), adds coverage.txt, and refactors AllPathsBetween in paths.go to use newStack[K]. It does NOT touch dag.go or traversal.go at all, and does not modify CreatesCycle in paths.go. Consequently, all three named walks still keep private inline stack implementations: TransitiveReduction still uses `pending = pending[:len(pending)-1]` with `onPending` map, DFS still uses `frontier = frontier[:len(frontier)-1]` with `queued` map, and CreatesCycle still uses `ancestors = ancestors[:len(ancestors)-1]` with `queued` map. None delegate their open-set discipline to a shared abstraction, so the rubric fails.
rubrics.criterion: Every production graph walk that today consumes its open vertex set with inline slice-end truncation plus a hand-rolled membership map (the frontier walks in the cycle check, the depth-first traversal, and the per-successor walk of the transitive reduction) delegates that open-set discipline to a shared internal abstraction at the package's usual level - the existing generic stack helper, a reintroduced helper, or an equally well-scoped owner - so no walk keeps a private stack implementation in its body.

No trace of either guard message or its wrapping survives in the patched AllPathsBetween.
